source_refs.note: Topic printed 1.1.1.1 Requirement Gathering (PDF 6, printed 3), part of 1.2.2's stages; the numbering is a print slip.

blocks.text: Requirement gathering is the initial phase of the SDLC. The goal is to understand and collect what the software needs to achieve, by talking to the people who will use it and to other stakeholders to find out their needs and expectations. For example, if you are developing a new app for a school, you might ask students, teachers and administrators what features they would like to see.

items: Interviews and surveys: asking questions and collecting feedback from potential users to understand their needs and preferences.
Observations: watching how users interact with current systems to identify problems and opportunities for improvement.
Document review: looking at existing documents, such as reports and user manuals, to gather more information about the requirements.

blocks.text: Requirement gathering is like planning a big event such as a wedding: just as you need to know the preferences of the bride and groom, developers need to know what the users want from the software (Did You Know).
